findings.description: wp-contracts' verification step runs only test_schema_copies.py, so the conftest fixture builder introduced by task 1.3 is first exercised by wp-registry and wp-resolver rather than by the package that ships it.
findings.resolution: Accepted: a smoke test for a fixture builder adds little; the dependent packages fail fast if it is wrong.

findings.description: The Ownership Check requirement enumerates only the map/registry error classes; the CODEOWNERS-class errors (missing_github_handle, codeowners_disagreement, not_a_git_checkout) are specified under CODEOWNERS Projection and cross-referenced through design D9's code table.
findings.resolution: Accepted: each error is normatively specified once; D9 is the single enumeration the --json contract points at.

findings.description: Tasks 5.4 and 5.5 (state-artifacts inventory row and its test) have no dependencies but sit in wp-dogfood-docs, which waits on wp-registry and wp-codeowners.
findings.resolution: Accepted: two S documentation tasks do not justify a seventh package; the implementer may run them first inside wp-dogfood-docs.

findings.description: The human-principals schema keeps an optional `email` field that no code in this change consumes (design D5); it exists for ri-03 attribution and is personal data a maintainer may prefer not to publish.
findings.resolution: Escalate to the human reviewer at approval: keep (schema stability for six later items) or strike until ri-03. Recorded as an open question in design.md and the session log.
